import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/training_5.csv"
]

# Columns expected in all source files (all have the same schema)
expected_columns = [
    'Timestamp [ms]', 'CPU cores', 'CPU capacity provisioned [MHZ]', 'CPU usage [MHZ]', 'CPU usage [%]',
    'Memory capacity provisioned [KB]', 'Memory usage [KB]', 'Disk read throughput [KB/s]',
    'Disk write throughput [KB/s]', 'Network received throughput [KB/s]', 'Network transmitted throughput [KB/s]'
]

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as expected (no missing or extra columns)
    df = df[expected_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target except the last column 'Timestamp' (string),
# and the target schema is the same columns plus the string 'Timestamp' column,
# we can union (concat) all source tables first.

combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Now, add the 'Timestamp' column (string) converted from 'Timestamp [ms]'
# 'Timestamp [ms]' is an integer representing Unix epoch time in seconds or milliseconds?
# From the example values (e.g., 1377500869), it looks like seconds since epoch (10 digits).
# But the column name says [ms], so it should be milliseconds.
# The example target Timestamp string is '2013-08-26 07:07:49' which corresponds to 1377500869 seconds.
# So the source 'Timestamp [ms]' is actually in seconds, not milliseconds, despite the name.
# We will treat it as seconds (divide by 1 if needed).

# To confirm, convert 'Timestamp [ms]' to datetime string:
# If it were milliseconds, dividing by 1000 would be needed.
# But the example target Timestamp string matches seconds.

# Let's convert 'Timestamp [ms]' as seconds since epoch to datetime string.

combined_df['Timestamp'] = combined_df['Timestamp [ms]'].apply(
    lambda x: datetime.utcfromtimestamp(int(x)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
)

# Ensure data types match target schema:
# Target schema:
# 'Timestamp [ms]': integer
# 'CPU cores': integer
# 'CPU capacity provisioned [MHZ]': float
# 'CPU usage [MHZ]': float
# 'CPU usage [%]': float
# 'Memory capacity provisioned [KB]': integer
# 'Memory usage [KB]': float
# 'Disk read throughput [KB/s]': integer
# 'Disk write throughput [KB/s]': float
# 'Network received throughput [KB/s]': float
# 'Network transmitted throughput [KB/s]': float
# 'Timestamp': string

# Convert columns accordingly:

combined_df['Timestamp [ms]'] = combined_df['Timestamp [ms]'].astype(int)
combined_df['CPU cores'] = combined_df['CPU cores'].astype(int)
combined_df['CPU capacity provisioned [MHZ]'] = combined_df['CPU capacity provisioned [MHZ]'].astype(float)
combined_df['CPU usage [MHZ]'] = combined_df['CPU usage [MHZ]'].astype(float)
combined_df['CPU usage [%]'] = combined_df['CPU usage [%]'].astype(float)
combined_df['Memory capacity provisioned [KB]'] = combined_df['Memory capacity provisioned [KB]'].astype(int)
combined_df['Memory usage [KB]'] = combined_df['Memory usage [KB]'].astype(float)
combined_df['Disk read throughput [KB/s]'] = combined_df['Disk read throughput [KB/s]'].astype(int)
combined_df['Disk write throughput [KB/s]'] = combined_df['Disk write throughput [KB/s]'].astype(float)
combined_df['Network received throughput [KB/s]'] = combined_df['Network received throughput [KB/s]'].astype(float)
combined_df['Network transmitted throughput [KB/s]'] = combined_df['Network transmitted throughput [KB/s]'].astype(float)
# 'Timestamp' is already string

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'Timestamp [ms]', 'CPU cores', 'CPU capacity provisioned [MHZ]', 'CPU usage [MHZ]', 'CPU usage [%]',
    'Memory capacity provisioned [KB]', 'Memory usage [KB]', 'Disk read throughput [KB/s]',
    'Disk write throughput [KB/s]', 'Network received throughput [KB/s]', 'Network transmitted throughput [KB/s]',
    'Timestamp'
]

combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
combined_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_22/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
